newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan property firms say worst of slump is over.
newsitem.headline: Japan property firms say worst of slump is over.

text.p: Major Japanese property firms, suffering from a prolonged real estate slump, said on Thursday the worst is over and the slump may be finally disappearing.
Mitsubishi Estate Co Ltd and Sumitomo Realty and Development Co Ltd unveiled steep falls in their earnings for last business year, ended in March, but both expect profit rises in the current year.
"I think we could say that the worst is over. We have already hit bottom," a Mitsubishi Estate spokesman said. He said office building leasing is on a steady recovery trend.

Mitsubishi Estate, suffering from falling profits for several years, said its 1996/97 parent current profit fell year-on-year 44.3 percent to 16.32 billion yen ($140 million) but expects its 1997/98 current profit will be almost unchanged at 17 billion yen ($146 million).
Current profit is pre-tax but includes gains and losses on securities investments and other non-operating activities.

Sumitomo, which reported a 76.1 percent fall in its parent current profit in 1996/97, said it expected current profit to grow sharply to 6.00 billion yen ($51.7 million) in 1997/98. Its 1996/97 parent current profit was 1.15 billion yen.

"In the current business year, the property industry will be more confident about its recovery as it will see further industry deregulation. The government is also likely to come up with various steps for the efficient use of land," Sumitomo Realty said in a statement.
"We are certain that office building business will continue its steady recovery and that sales of condominiums (apartments) will be firm as we expect low interest rates to continue," it said.
On Thursday, hopes that urban land prices had bottomed out lifted share prices of property firms in the Tokyo market.
"Investors are acting favourably about some media reports that the government will announce its view on Friday that falls in residential land prices have stopped," a Tokyo trader said.
The National Land Agency said it will announce its views on land prices on Friday, without elaborating further.

Mitsubishi Estate shares closed up 20 yen at 1,660 yen and Sumitomo Realty ended up 26 yen at 969 yen on Thursday on the Tokyo Stock Exchange. Shares of another major realtor Mitsui Fudosan Co Ltd closed at 1,500 yen, up 30 yen. ($1=116 yen)
